title: Algebraic description of complex conjugation on cohomology of a smooth projective hypersurface

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, paragraph after the comparison isomorphism \(I_\sigma\)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: It claims that \(1\otimes c\) on the de Rham side corresponds to \(\iota_\sigma\otimes c\) on the Betti side. This contradicts the earlier statement that \((H_B\otimes C)^{1\otimes c}\cong H_B\otimes R\) and the later definition of \(c_{dR}\) as corresponding to \(1\otimes c\) on the Betti side. The algebraic de Rham comparison over a real embedding maps real algebraic forms to real Betti cohomology, which is fixed by \(1\otimes c\), not by \(\iota_\sigma\otimes c\).

The theorem asserts \(\varphi_C([y^i f_{j_i}(x)]) = \varphi_C([y^{n-1-i} \tilde f_{j_i}(x)])\) without complex conjugation. The left side lies in \(H^{n-1-i,i}\) and the right side in \(H^{i,n-1-i}\), so equality in the direct sum \(H_0\) would force both to be zero, contradicting the choice of nonzero basis classes. It should involve \(\overline{\varphi_C([y^i f_{j_i}(x)])}\).

For a symmetric intersection matrix \(P\), Poincaré duality gives \(\int_X \omega\wedge\bar\omega = a P^{-1}\bar a^T\), where \(a_i=\int_{\gamma_i}\omega\). The paper instead uses \(P_X P \overline{P_X}^T\), i.e. \(a P \bar a^T\). Since \(P^{-1}\neq P\) generally, e.g. for a rank-one block \([d]\) with \(d\neq 1\), this formula is wrong.

For a conjugate Hodge pair \(H^{p,q}\oplus H^{q,p}\), the real subspace fixed by conjugation is spanned by \((v+\bar v)/2\) and \((v-\bar v)/(2i)\), not by \(w=(v+\bar v)/2\) and \(i w\). The vector \(i w\) is anti-fixed by conjugation. Thus the expression \(R[w]+R[\sqrt{-1}w]\) does not describe the real cohomology. In Example 2.8, it corresponds to \(R\,dx + R\,i\,dx\), not \(R\,dx+R\,dy\).

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Theorem 2.3, displayed isomorphism \(H_0\to H_{2m+1}\)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proof states that the isomorphism is given by \(\omega\mapsto \sum_i (\int_{\gamma_i}\omega)\gamma_i\) for a canonical symplectic basis. For the symplectic matrix \(Q=\begin{pmatrix}0&I\\-I&0\end{pmatrix}\), the Poincaré dual of the dual class \(\gamma_1^*\) is \(-\gamma_{1+g}\), not \(\gamma_1\). The coefficients require \(Q^{-1}\).

The numerator is written as \(\int_{\gamma_1}\omega \cdot \int_{\gamma_2}\omega - \int_{\gamma_2}\omega \cdot \int_{\gamma_1}\omega\), which is identically zero. It should contain complex conjugates on the second factors, as in Definition 2.2, otherwise \(\mu=0\) and the later formula for the real cohomology collapses.

The expression \(\lfloor |I_m|+1/2\rfloor\) equals \(|I_m|\) for every integer \(|I_m|\), which conflicts with the intended selection of roughly half of the self-conjugate middle component. The intended notation is almost certainly \(\lfloor (|I_m|+1)/2\rfloor\).

It states that \(\{[1],[y u(x)]\}\) is a \(\mathbb{Q}\)-basis of \(\mathbb{Q}[y,x]/\mathrm{Jac}(S)\). The full quotient is infinite-dimensional; these two classes span only the charge-zero part \(A_0/(\mathrm{Jac}(S)\cap A_0)\).

The proof writes \(\mathcal{C}(\phi_C(U_k),\phi_C(U_k)) = \int_X \phi_C(U_k)\wedge \overline{\phi_C(U_k)}\), but \(\mathcal{C}(w,w')\) was defined as \(\int_X w\wedge w'\). The second argument should be \(\overline{\phi_C(U_k)}\). Similarly, 'finding \(\phi_C^{-1}(\phi_C(U_k))\)' should be finding \(\phi_C^{-1}(\overline{\phi_C(U_k)})\).

For \(|I_m|\) even, the stated expression sums over all \(j\in I_m\) with two real dimensions per index, giving real dimension \(2\sum_{i=0}^{m}|I_i|\), whereas \(H^{2m}_{prim}(X,R)\) has real dimension \(2\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}|I_i|+|I_m|\). For \(|I_m|\) odd and greater than 1, the stated expression also has excess real dimension.
